data.name: Emmaus
data.gender_notes: Emmaus is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In the New Testament, Emmaus refers to a village where Jesus appeared to two of His disciples after His Resurrection. This name symbolizes the place where one experiences a profound spiritual revelation. The name Emmaus carries the meaning “Place of revelation” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Emmaus usually hope their child will grow to embody place of revelation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A place of divine encounter and spiritual awakening
data.etymology: Emmaus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Place of revelation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Emmaus total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: עמאוס
in_hebrew.meaning: מקום שם האבות, שם שם צדיק
in_hebrew.long_meaning: בתחילה, עמאוס היה שם של עיר בארץ יהודה (יוחנן 20:19), ואחר כך הפך לשם פרטי. על פי המסורת, עמאוס הוא מקום שם האבות, כלומר שם של צדיק, שנקרא 'עמאוס' כבודו. בספר יוחנן, עמאוס הוא שם של שני אנשים שהיו חסידים ואמנויים, שפגשו את ישו לאחר הגביע. השם 'עמאוס' מציין את החשיבות והכבוד שניתן לעם ישראל, וגם את החשיבות של האמונה והדת ביהדות.

in_greek.name: Ἐμμαοῦς
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἐμμαοῦς ἦταν πόλις ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ (Ἰωάννου 20:19). Ἐπιτέλους ἔγινε ὄνομα προσωπικό. Ἐν τῇ Ἰωάννῳ, Ἐμμαοῦς ἦταν ὄνομα δύο ἀνδρῶν οἵτινες ἦσαν δίκαιοι καὶ ὑπῆρχον ἐν ὑπομονή. Ἐν τῇ Ἰωάννῳ 20:19, Ἐμμαοῦς εἶναι τὸ ὄνομα τῶν δύο ἀνδρῶν οἵτινες εἶδον τὸν Ἰησοῦν μετὰ τὴν κρίσιν. Ἐξ οὐσιαστικῶς, Ἐμμαοῦς δηλώνει τὸν τοποθεσία ὃν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα, καὶ τὴν ὑποδοχὴ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων. Ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ, Ἐμμαοῦς εἶναι τὸ ὄνομα τῆς πόλεως ἡ ὁποία εἶχε τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρός.

in_latin.name: Emmaus
in_latin.long_meaning: Emmaus erat nomen urbis in Judaea (Ioannes 20:19). Postea factum est nomen proprium. In Ioanne, Emmaus erat nomen duorum virorum qui erant justi et patientes. In Ioanne 20:19, Emmaus est nomen duorum virorum qui viderunt Iesum post condemnationem. In essentia, Emmaus significat locum ubi nomen patris, et acceptatio Iesu a hominibus. In Judaea, Emmaus erat nomen urbis quae habebat nomen patris.

in_english.name: Emmaus
in_english.meaning: place of the father's name, town of the righteous
in_english.long_meaning: Initially, Emmaus was the name of a town in Judaea (John 20:19), and later it became a personal name. In the Gospel of John, Emmaus is the name of two righteous men who were patient and faithful, and who saw Jesus after the crucifixion. The name Emmaus signifies the place of the father's name, and the acceptance of Jesus by men. In Christian tradition, Emmaus is a name that symbolizes the importance of faith and the father's name.

data.cultural_impact: The name Emmaus has become synonymous with spiritual awakening and enlightenment. It is a reminder of the transformative power of an encounter with the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: The village of Emmaus holds deep spiritual significance for Christians. It represents the place where the disciples, in their confusion and doubt after Jesus' crucifixion, found their faith renewed through the Risen Lord's presence. Thus, it serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and embracing the presence of God in our lives, even in times of darkness and uncertainty.
